criteria.Expected check: Identify the corresponding Material 3 type and supported variants.
Compare public configuration, content slots, and composition.
Compare parts, dimensions, alignment, spacing, and icon placement.
Verify the applicable Material target geometry.
Verify semantic container, content, border, and state colors in light mode.
Verify semantic container, content, border, and state colors in dark mode.
Verify family, scale role, size, line height, weight, and tracking.
Verify corners, padding, gaps, borders, tonal and shadow elevation.
Verify resting visual and behavior.
Verify hover state with hover-capable pointer.
Verify keyboard focus indicator and focus behavior.
Verify active/pressed treatment and release behavior.
Verify selected or checked state where applicable.
Verify disabled visual, focus, and activation behavior.
Verify validation and error presentation where applicable.
Verify pending feedback and geometry where applicable.
Verify read-only semantics where applicable.
Verify expanded, open, or dragged states where applicable.
Verify pointer, touch, gesture, and cancellation behavior.
Verify keyboard controls and native form behavior.
Verify name, role, state, focus order, and screen reader output.
Verify contextual contrast and non-color cues.
Verify duration, easing, direction, and animated properties.
Verify enter/exit and interrupted transitions where applicable.
Verify reduced-motion behavior.
Verify compact, medium, expanded, and boundary conditions as applicable.
Verify zoom, long content, overflow, and RTL layout.
Verify light/dark, dynamic color, custom theme, and scoped overrides.
Verify empty/long content, icon-only content, and localization.
Verify overlays, stacking, scrolling, and nested use where applicable.
Verify supported browsers, SSR/hydration, layout stability, and performance as applicable.
Link updated docs, source, unit/browser tests, and visual evidence.
Native implementation consumes supported Material component and system roles directly; scoped overrides reach the rendered element.
Native CSS and behavior work without the Core theme bridge or legacy token declarations; shared Core utilities have an evidenced semantic match.
Anatomy, defaults, variants, sizes and states follow the pinned Material source; Core compatibility lives in a separate entry point.
Legacy exports and aliases delegate toward the native implementation without cycles or a second independently maintained value map.
The published native entry point renders in docsite and Storybook with source, status and exact revision visible for human QA.
Pinned Compose governs overlapping design, behavior and motion; missing concerns and approved exceptions are recorded once per family. Figma-only coverage and native web semantics remain required.
Reference and native captures use matched conditions; exact pixel diff passes or a reviewed tolerance exception is recorded.
Watched reference media, timed frames, interruption, reversal and reduced motion are evidenced, or static behavior has a source-backed N/A.
Pinned Compose defaults, variants and relevant test cases are mapped to permanent web tests; differences and missing upstream coverage are explicit.
Recorded browser/device profiles meet the approved input response and frame pacing budgets, including active motion and interruption.

decisions: Resolved baseline required; code and interactive QA remain pending.
